comments.text:
This is the first zone of Act 3 after Moonrise, and the coronation takes place at the entrance to Baldur's Gate. Disabling dynamic crowds (which causes civilian characters to either flee combat or attend performances) or using slow HDD mode didn't improve performance. I first noticed performance degradation during the initial fight in the Shadow Curse of Act 2, but it was manageable.

These numbers are based on Patch 2, Hotfix 5, using a Ryzen 5800H at 3.9GHz and a 3060 with the latest drivers in DX11 with all ultra, and observations made with Nvidia overlay with a static camera.

In Act 1 river camp, GPU bottleneck at 1080p with DLAA, 80fps avg with 66fps 1% lows. Without DLAA, the performance improved to 90fps avg with 78fps 1% lows.

In the Emerald Grove Druid Circle, looking west from the rock arch, CPU bottleneck at 1080p DLSS Quality, 66fps avg with 57fps 1% lows.

In Act 2, at the Last Light Inn waypoint, looking North East, CPU bottleneck at 1080p with DLAA, 51fps avg with 43fps 1% lows. Same with DLSS Performance.

In Act 3, at the South Span Bridge gate, looking north, CPU bottleneck at 1620p with DLAA, 41fps avg 35fps 1% lows. With 720p DLSS Performance, marginal improvement to 44fps avg with 37fps 1% lows.

Inside the Coronation Audience hall, looking north, CPU bottleneck at 1620p with DLAA, 23fps avg with 21fps 1% lows. Same with 720p DLSS Performance. Regular single-digit stutters along with GPU spikes.

In the Lower City, at the Basilisk Gate waypoint, looking at the gallows, CPU bottleneck at 1080p with DLAA, 39fps with 32fps 1% lows. Same numbers without DLAA and with 720p DLSS Performance at low graphics preset. This might be the first game to truely benefit from DLFG or something similar.  @TechTesters
